subject: Web Development
title: WebAssembly: Native Speed in the Browser
description: A short lesson to help you apply WebAssembly: Native Speed in the Browser.

hook.text: JavaScript is fast, but it can't match the speed of C++ or Rust for heavy computation.

buildup.text: WebAssembly (Wasm) lets you run compiled code at near-native speed inside the browser.

discovery.text: Games, video editors, and CAD tools now run in a browser tab without plugins.

twist.text: Wasm isn't replacing JavaScript. They work together — JS for UI, Wasm for heavy lifting.

climax.text: WebAssembly turns the browser into a universal runtime for any programming language.

punchline.text: Any language can now run in any browser.
